executive_summary: Across Q1–Q4 FY26, MPS delivered margin-led earnings growth despite uneven revenue, with FY26 becoming its most profitable year ever (30.7% EBITDA margin). Management executed a deliberate reset—pruning AJE revenues, restructuring Corporate Learning, and doubling down on AI-first workflows—culminating in strong Q4 momentum and confident FY27 EBITDA guidance (>₹300 cr). The Unbound Medicine acquisition marks a strategic expansion into recurring, regulated healthcare knowledge platforms. Overall, management credibility is supported by consistent margin delivery, transparent acknowledgement of missteps (AJE, Corporate Learning), and increasingly specific forward commitments.

evidence: Q1FY26: Management acknowledged a 'soft start' and explicitly called out AJE as an overhang rather than masking weakness.
Q2FY26: Rahul Arora stated Corporate Learning had been a 'soft year' and framed FY26 as a restructuring/reset year.
Q4FY26: Management gave explicit EBITDA guidance for FY27 (>₹300 cr) and stated it was 'built bottom-up' and already in execution.
Feb2026 (Unbound call): Clear, quantified margin ramp guidance for Unbound (14% to MPS average by FY27 exit), showing confidence and specificity.
Q4FY26: Capital allocation explanation (no final dividend due to deployment cycle) was candid and principle-based.

guidance_evolution.pattern_summary: Management generally sets conservative-to-realistic targets, openly resets narratives when needed (AJE, Corporate Learning), and then delivers on revised expectations rather than silently deferring.

margin_commentary: Margins were the central management focus across quarters. Management consistently cited AI-driven automation, workflow redesign, offshoring, and portfolio pruning as margin levers. Credibility is high: EBITDA margins expanded from ~28–31% in early FY26 to 32.9% in Q4 and 30.7% for FY26, validating repeated claims that AI and operating leverage would structurally lift margins.
revenue_growth_narrative: Revenue growth in FY26 was uneven and largely margin-sacrificed in AJE and Corporate Learning, while Education saw strong organic growth (28–60%). The narrative shifted from acquisition-led scale to disciplined, AI-enabled organic expansion plus selective, higher-quality M&A (Unbound). This shift has been consistent since mid-FY26.
key_risks_flagged_by_management: Corporate Learning softness and restructuring risk (Q1FY26, Q2FY26).
AJE revenue volatility during margin reset (Q1FY26, Q2FY26).
Execution risk in integrating acquisitions and scaling AI responsibly in regulated workflows (Q4FY26, Feb2026).
positive_signals: FY26 highest-ever EBITDA (₹236 cr) and EPS (₹102) – Q4FY26.
Education segment delivered 36%+ organic growth with ~39% EBITDA margin – Q4FY26.
Unbound Medicine added recurring revenue and new healthcare vertical – Feb2026.
DSO improvement from ~60 days to ~37–45 days – Q1–Q2FY26.
Clear FY27 EBITDA guidance (>₹300 cr) – Q4FY26.
red_flags: Repeated deferral of revenue growth recovery at AJE until FY27 (Q1–Q4FY26).
Corporate Learning turnaround took longer than initially suggested (Q1 vs Q2FY26).
Limited revenue disclosure on Unbound initially, citing account closure timing (Feb2026).

business_problems_and_challenges.problem: Difficulty scaling Corporate Learning profitably due to commoditized compliance content and fragmented delivery.
business_problems_and_challenges.evidence: Management described FY26 as a 'reset year' and exited low-margin compliance work (Q2FY26, Q4FY26).

business_problems_and_challenges.problem: Need for reliable AI verification and integrity checks in scholarly publishing workflows.
business_problems_and_challenges.evidence: Repeated emphasis that the bottleneck has shifted from content generation to verification (Q4FY26).

overall_investment_signal: positive: Margin execution, AI monetisation, and disciplined capital allocation underpin confidence, though revenue acceleration still needs to prove consistency post-FY26 reset.
